body.translated_text: Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s>. [1.1.1]
[<s>Brahman</s> is that] from which the origin etc. of this [universe proceed]. [1.1.2]
Because scripture is its source [of knowledge]. [1.1.3]
But that [<s>Brahman</s> is known from scripture], because of the harmony [of all scriptural passages]. [1.1.4]
Because of [the mention of] seeing (<s>īkṣaṇa</s>), [the cause of the world] is not the non-sentient [<s>pradhāna</s>]. [1.1.5]
[If it be said that the reference is] secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>), [we say] no, because of the word 'Self' (<s>ātman</s>). [1.1.6]
Because liberation is taught for one who is devoted to that [<s>Brahman</s>]. [1.1.7]
And because there is no statement of [its] being something to be rejected. [1.1.8]
Because of the contradiction with the proposition. [1.1.9]
Because of [the soul's] merging [into <s>Brahman</s> in deep sleep]. [1.1.10]
Because of the uniformity of [scriptural] teaching. [1.1.11]
And because it is so heard [in scripture]. [1.1.12]
The one consisting of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>) [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of repetition. [1.1.13]

body.text: vikāraśabdān neti cen na prācuryāt | BBs_1,1.14 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said] 'no,' because of the word denoting modification—[we say] no, because of abundance [of bliss]. [1.1.14]
And because [<s>Brahman</s>] is declared to be the cause of that [bliss]. [1.1.15]
What is stated in the <s>mantra</s> verses alone is sung [here too]. [1.1.16]
Not the other [individual soul], because of the impossibility [of the attributes applying to it]. [1.1.17]
And because of the declaration of difference [between the individual soul and <s>Brahman</s>]. [1.1.18]
And because of [the fulfillment of] desire, no dependence on inference is [needed]. [1.1.19]

body.text: asminn asya ca tadyogaṃ śāsti | BBs_1,1.20 |
body.translated_text: [Scripture] teaches the connection of this [individual soul] with that [<s>Brahman</s>] in this [context]. [1.1.20]
[<s>Brahman</s> is the being] within, because of the teaching of its attributes. [1.1.21]
And [it is] another [i.e., <s>Brahman</s>, not the individual soul], because of the declaration of difference. [1.1.22]
[The word] '<s>ākāśa</s>' [means <s>Brahman</s>], because of its characteristic marks. [1.1.23]
For the same reason, [the word] '<s>prāṇa</s>' [also means <s>Brahman</s>]. [1.1.24]
'Light' (<s>jyotis</s>) [means <s>Brahman</s>], because of the mention of feet (<s>caraṇa</s>). [1.1.25]

body.text: chando 'bhidhānān neti cen na tathā ceto'rpaṇanigadāt tathā hi darśanam | BBs_1,1.26 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said] 'no,' because of the mention of metre (<s>chandas</s>)—[we say] no, because [the instruction is] thus about directing the mind; for so is it seen [in scripture]. [1.1.26]
And because of the aptness of the description in terms of elements etc. [it is] thus. [1.1.27]

body.text: upadeśabhedān neti cen nobhayasminn apy avirodhāt | BBs_1,1.28 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said] 'no,' because of the difference in teaching—[we say] no, because there is no contradiction in either [interpretation]. [1.1.28]
'<s>Prāṇa</s>' [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the tracing [of everything back to it]. [1.1.29]

body.text: na vaktur ātmopadeśād iti ced adhyātmasaṃbandhabhūmā hy asmin | BBs_1,1.30 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said] 'no,' because of the teaching about the speaker's own self—[truly] there is an abundance of references to the inner self in this [passage]. [1.1.30]
But the instruction is from the standpoint of scripture, as in the case of <s>Vāmadeva</s>. [1.1.31]

body.text: jīvamukhyaprāṇaliṅgān neti cen nopāsātraividhyādāśritatvād iha tadyogāt | BBs_1,1.32 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said that <s>Brahman</s> is] not [meant], because of the marks of the individual soul, the chief vital breath, and [other entities]—[we say] no, because of the threefold nature of meditation, and because it is here resorted to, and because of the connection with that [<s>Brahman</s>] here. [1.1.32]
[<s>Brahman</s> is meant] because of the well-known teaching everywhere. [1.2.1]
And because of the aptness of the qualities intended [to be expressed]. [1.2.2]
But [it is] not the embodied [individual soul], because of impossibility. [1.2.3]
And because of the designation [of <s>Brahman</s>] as both the object and the agent of action. [1.2.4]
Because of the distinctive word [used]. [1.2.5]
And because of <s>smṛti</s> (tradition). [1.2.6]

body.text: arbhakaustvāt tadvyapadeśāc ca neti cen na nicāyyatvād evaṃ vyomavac ca | BBs_1,2.7 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said that <s>Brahman</s> is not meant] because of [its] smallness and because of the designation as such—[we say] no, because it is to be understood thus, and because [it is] like space (<s>vyoman</s>). [1.2.7]

body.text: saṃbhogaprāptir iti cen na vaiśeṣyāt | BBs_1,2.8 |
body.translated_text: If [it be objected that] the attainment of enjoyment [would follow]—[we say] no, because of the distinction [between <s>Brahman</s> and the individual soul]. [1.2.8]
The eater [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the reference to both the moving and non-moving [being consumed]. [1.2.9]
And because of the context. [1.2.10]

body.text: guhāṃ praviṣṭāv ātmānau hi taddarśanāt | BBs_1,2.11 |
body.translated_text: The two who have entered the cave are indeed the [individual] selves, for that is seen [in scripture]. [1.2.11]
And because of the qualifying [descriptions]. [1.2.12]
The one within [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of fitness. [1.2.13]
And because of the designation of place etc. [1.2.14]
And because of the description as distinguished by bliss. [1.2.15]

body.text: ata eva ca sa brahma | BBs_1,2.16 |
body.translated_text: For this very reason, he is <s>Brahman</s>. [1.2.16]
And because of the mention of the path [attained by those who] have heard the <s>Upaniṣad</s>. [1.2.17]
Not the other [i.e., individual soul or <s>pradhāna</s>], because of the impossibility of abiding and of non-existence [of the attributes]. [1.2.18]
[<s>Brahman</s> is] the inner ruler (<s>antaryāmin</s>) in the divine, cosmic, and other [spheres], because of the designation of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] attributes. [1.2.19]

body.text: na ca smārtam ataddharmābhilāpāc chārīraś ca | BBs_1,2.20 |
body.translated_text: And [it is] not what is known from <s>smṛti</s> [i.e., <s>pradhāna</s>], because of the declaration of attributes not belonging to it; and [it is not] the embodied [soul either]. [1.2.20]
For both [Śākha] recensions read of him with the distinction [from the individual soul]. [1.2.21]
[<s>Brahman</s> possesses] the attributes of invisibility etc., because of the declaration of [its] qualities. [1.2.22]
And not the other two [<s>pradhāna</s> and individual soul], because of the specification and the declaration of difference. [1.2.23]
And because of the description of form. [1.2.24]
<s>Vaiśvānara</s> [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the common and specific terms. [1.2.25]
What is remembered [in <s>smṛti</s>] may be taken as an inference. [1.2.26]

body.text: śabdādibhyo 'ntaḥpratiṣṭhānāc ca neti cen na tathā dṛṣṭyupadeśād asambhavāt puruṣamapi cainam adhīyate | BBs_1,2.27 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said] 'no,' because of [the reference to] word etc. and [its] being established within—[we say] no, because thus the meditation is taught, and because of the impossibility [otherwise]; and he is also read of as a person (<s>puruṣa</s>). [1.2.27]

body.text: ata eva na devatā bhūtaṃ ca | BBs_1,2.28 |
body.translated_text: For this very reason, [<s>Vaiśvānara</s>] is neither a deity nor an element. [1.2.28]
<s>Jaimini</s> [holds that] even the direct [identification] is not contradictory. [1.2.29]
[It is] because of manifestation, says <s>Āśmarathya</s>. [1.2.30]
[It is] because of remembrance, [says] <s>Bādari</s>. [1.2.31]

body.text: saṃpatter iti jaiminis tathā hi darśayati | BBs_1,2.32 |
body.translated_text: [It is] because of identification, [says] <s>Jaimini</s>; for so [scripture] shows. [1.2.32]
And they acknowledge him in this [context]. [1.2.33]
That which has heaven, earth, etc. as its abode [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of its own word. [1.3.1]
And because of the designation as that which is to be approached by the liberated. [1.3.2]
[It is] not [the <s>pradhāna</s> inferred by] <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, because of the absence of that term; and because it sustains life (<s>prāṇabhṛt</s>). [1.3.3]
Because of the declaration of difference. [1.3.4]
Because of the context. [1.3.5]
And because of [the mention of its] abiding and eating. [1.3.6]
<s>Bhūman</s> (the Infinite) [is <s>Brahman</s>], because it is taught beyond <s>saṃprasāda</s> (serenity). [1.3.7]
And because of the fitness of the attributes [described]. [1.3.8]
The Imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the support of everything up to <s>ākāśa</s>. [1.3.9]
And that [support is from <s>Brahman</s>] because of [its] command. [1.3.10]
And because of the exclusion of all other natures. [1.3.11]
That [is <s>Brahman</s>], because it is designated as the object of the act of seeing (<s>īkṣati</s>). [1.3.12]
The small [space within the heart] (<s>dahara</s>) [is <s>Brahman</s>], from what follows [in the text]. [1.3.13]

body.text: gatiśabdābhyāṃ tathā hi dṛṣṭaṃ liṅgaṃ ca | BBs_1,3.14 |
body.translated_text: Because of [the words] 'going' and 'word,' and for thus is the mark seen [in scripture]. [1.3.14]
And because of the holding and because its greatness is perceived in this [context]. [1.3.15]
And because of the well-known [meaning]. [1.3.16]

body.text: itaraparāmarśāt sa iti cen nāsaṃbhavāt | BBs_1,3.17 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said that] it [the small space] refers to the other [individual soul]—[we say] no, because of impossibility. [1.3.17]
But if [it be argued] from what follows [that the individual soul is meant]—his revealed nature [refers to liberation]. [1.3.18]
And the reference [to the individual soul] serves another purpose. [1.3.19]

body.text: alpaśruter iti cet tad uktam | BBs_1,3.20 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said that <s>Brahman</s> is not meant] because of the brief [teaching]—that has [already] been answered. [1.3.20]
And because of imitation of that [<s>Brahman</s>]. [1.3.21]
Moreover, [it is] remembered [in <s>smṛti</s>]. [1.3.22]
[<s>Brahman</s> is] known from the word [of scripture] alone. [1.3.23]
But [the meditation on <s>Brahman</s> is to be performed] in the heart, since human beings alone are entitled [to such knowledge]. [1.3.24]
<s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds that the gods] also [are entitled to knowledge], because of the possibility. [1.3.25]

body.text: virodhaḥ karmaṇīti cen nānekapratipatter darśanāt | BBs_1,3.26 |
body.translated_text: If [it be objected that there is] a contradiction with [Vedic ritual] action—[we say] no, because of the observation that multiple [capacities are] possible. [1.3.26]

body.text: śabda iti cen nātaḥ prabhavāt pratyakṣānumānābhyām | BBs_1,3.27 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said] because of [the Veda being] word [it is eternal]—[we say] no, because [the world] originates from that; [and this is known] from perception and inference. [1.3.27]
And for this very reason, [the Veda's] eternality [is established]. [1.3.28]
And because of the sameness of names and forms [in each creation cycle], there is no contradiction even in the repetition [of creation]; as is seen [in scripture] and [in] <s>smṛti</s>. [1.3.29]
<s>Jaimini</s> [holds that] there is no entitlement [to knowledge for the gods] because of the impossibility [of performing meditations on] honey etc. [1.3.30]
And because of [the god's] being in the [sacrificial] fire. [1.3.31]
But <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> [holds that] there is [entitlement], for [the gods] do exist. [1.3.32]

body.text: śugasya tadanādaraśravaṇāt tadādravaṇāt sūcyate hi | BBs_1,3.33 |
body.translated_text: [The entitlement] of [one in] grief is indicated because of hearing [the scripture] without regard [to qualification], and because of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] rushing toward [such a one]; for [the scripture] suggests [this]. [1.3.33]
And because the attainment of <s>kṣatriya</s>-hood [is possible for one of another class]. [1.3.34]
And later, by the mark of [the story of] <s>Citraratha</s>. [1.3.35]
Because of the reference to [Vedic] purificatory rites, and because of the mention of their absence. [1.3.36]
And because of the determination of the absence of that [qualification], there is engagement [in knowledge]. [1.3.37]
Because of the prohibition of hearing and studying [for those without initiation]. [1.3.38]
And because of <s>smṛti</s>. [1.3.39]
Because of trembling [being mentioned in relation to <s>Brahman</s>]. [1.3.40]
'Light' [is <s>Brahman</s>], as is seen [in the context]. [1.3.41]
'<s>Ākāśa</s>' [is <s>Brahman</s>], because of the designation as something different [from the physical ākāśa] etc. [1.3.42]
[<s>Brahman</s> is distinct from the individual soul] by the distinction in deep sleep and departure. [1.3.43]
Because of the terms 'lord' (<s>pati</s>) etc. [1.3.44]

body.text: ānumānikam apy ekeṣām iti cen na śarīra-rūpaka-vinyasta-gṛhīter darśayati ca | BBs_1,4.1 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said that] even [the entity] inferred [by the Sāṃkhyas is mentioned] by some [Vedic schools]—[we say] no, because [it is a] figurative representation [of the body]; and [the scripture] shows [this]. [1.4.1]
But [the <s>pradhāna</s> is] subtle, because it is fit [to be so described]. [1.4.2]
Because it depends on that [<s>Brahman</s>], [the mention of <s>pradhāna</s>] has a purpose. [1.4.3]
And because there is no statement of [its] being an object of knowledge. [1.4.4]

body.text: vadatīti cen na prājño hi prakaraṇāt | BBs_1,4.5 |
body.translated_text: If [it be said that <s>pradhāna</s>] 'speaks'—[we say] no, because [the speaker] is the intelligent one, as [is clear] from the context. [1.4.5]

body.text: trayāṇām eva caivam upanyāsaḥ praśnaś ca | BBs_1,4.6 |
body.translated_text: And [the mention of] only three [entities is] thus, as shown by the exposition and the question. [1.4.6]
And [it is] like [the mention of] the 'great' (<s>mahat</s>). [1.4.7]
Like the bowls (<s>camasa</s>), because of non-distinction. [1.4.8]

body.text: jyotirupakramā tu tathā hy adhīyata eke | BBs_1,4.9 |
body.translated_text: But [the passage beginning with] 'light' (<s>jyoti</s>) [refers to <s>Brahman</s>], for so some read [in their recensions]. [1.4.9]
And because of the teaching through imagining, there is no contradiction, as in [the meditation on] honey etc. [1.4.10]

body.text: na saṃkhyopasaṃgrahādapi jñānābhāvād atirekāc ca | BBs_1,4.11 |
body.translated_text: Not even by inclusion [in] number [can <s>pradhāna</s> be accepted], because of the absence of [proper] knowledge and because of excess [of categories]. [1.4.11]
<s>Prāṇa</s> and others [are created from <s>Brahman</s>], because of the remainder of the sentence. [1.4.12]
By 'light,' [some schools understand the creation to begin], when food [is absent]. [1.4.13]
And as the cause [<s>Brahman</s>] is described in [the creation of] <s>ākāśa</s> and others, as stated. [1.4.14]
Because of the drawing together [of all passages]. [1.4.15]
Because [the term denotes] the world. [1.4.16]
If [it be said that <s>Brahman</s> is not meant] because of the marks of the individual soul, the chief vital breath, etc.—that has [already] been explained. [1.4.17]

body.text: anyārthaṃ tu jaiminiḥ praśnavyākhyānābhyām api caivam eke | BBs_1,4.18 |
body.translated_text: But <s>Jaimini</s> [holds that the passage] has another purpose, as shown by the question and the explanation; and some [schools] too [hold] thus. [1.4.18]
Because of the syntactical connection of the sentences. [1.4.19]
[The characteristic mark is] an indication of the fulfillment of the proposition, [says] <s>Āśmarathya</s>. [1.4.20]

body.text: utkramiṣyata evaṃ bhāvād ity auḍulomiḥ | BBs_1,4.21 |
body.translated_text: [The soul] will depart [from the body] in this manner, [says] <s>Auḍulomi</s>. [1.4.21]
Because of [the soul's] abiding [in the body], [says] <s>Kāśakṛtsna</s>. [1.4.22]
And [<s>Brahman</s>] is the source (<s>prakṛti</s>), so as not to contradict the proposition and the illustration. [1.4.23]
And because of the teaching of meditation (<s>abhidhyā</s>). [1.4.24]
And directly, because both [<s>Śruti</s> passages] declare [<s>Brahman</s> to be the cause]. [1.4.25]
Because [the world] is the creation of the Self. [1.4.26]
Because of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). [1.4.27]
And because [<s>Brahman</s>] is sung as the womb (source). [1.4.28]
By this, all [other views] are explained—explained. [1.4.29]

If [it be said that the acceptance of <s>Brahman</s> as cause leads to] the fault of there being no scope for other <s>smṛtis</s>—[we say] no, because there would equally be the fault of no scope for other <s>smṛtis</s> [in any view]. [2.1.1]
And because of the non-apprehension of the others [i.e., the categories of other systems are not perceived]. [2.1.2]
By this, [the system of] <s>Yoga</s> is also refuted. | BBs 2.1.3 |

body.text: na vilakṣaṇatvād asya tathātvaṃ ca śabdāt | BBs_2,1.4 |
body.translated_text: [The world is] not [independently real] because of its different character from [<s>Brahman</s>]; and that it is so [i.e., non-different] is [known] from scripture. | BBs 2.1.4 |
But the designation of [elements as] self-conscious [is] due to [their] association with [beings possessing] particular [consciousness]. | BBs 2.1.5 |
But it is observed [that effects differ from their causes]. | BBs 2.1.6 |

body.text: asad iti cen na pratiṣedhamātratvāt | BBs_2,1.7 |
body.translated_text: If [one says the world] is non-existent [before creation] — no, because [the scriptural passage involves] mere negation [of the effect's separate name and form]. | BBs 2.1.7 |
If at dissolution also there would be the same consequence [of <s>Brahman</s> becoming defective], [the objection is] untenable. | BBs 2.1.8 |
But not [so], because of the absence of a [suitable] analogy. | BBs 2.1.9 |
And because of the defect in [the objector's] own position. | BBs 2.1.10 |
Also because reasoning has no firm foundation. | BBs 2.1.11 |

body.text: anyathānumeyam iti ced evam apy anirmokṣaprasaṅgaḥ | BBs_2,1.12 |
body.translated_text: If [one says it] should be inferred otherwise, even so there would be the consequence of non-liberation. | BBs 2.1.12 |
By this, the [systems] not accepted by the learned are also explained [as refuted]. | BBs 2.1.13 |

body.text: bhoktrāpatter avibhāgaś cet syāl lokavat | BBs_2,1.14 |
body.translated_text: If [one objects that] there would be non-distinction [between <s>Brahman</s> and the individual soul] because the experiencer is implied — [we say] it would be as in the world. | BBs 2.1.14 |
The non-difference of that [effect from the cause is established] from the words 'origination' (<s>ārambhaṇa</s>) and others [in scripture]. | BBs 2.1.15 |
And because [the cause] is apprehended in the existence [of the effect]. | BBs 2.1.16 |
And because of the existence of the latter [cause in the effect]. | BBs 2.1.17 |

body.text: asadvyapadeśān neti cen na dharmāntareṇa vākyaśeṣādyukteḥ śabdāntarāc ca | BBs_2,1.18 |
body.translated_text: If [one says] 'not so, because [the effect] is designated as non-existent' — no, because [it is called non-existent] in a different sense, as [shown by] the remainder of the sentence, reasoning, and other scriptural passages. | BBs 2.1.18 |
And like a cloth [which is non-different from its threads]. | BBs 2.1.19 |
And as in the case of <s>prāṇa</s> and others. | BBs 2.1.20 |
If the other [i.e., <s>Brahman</s>] is designated [as the material cause], then faults such as purposelessness etc. would follow. | BBs 2.1.21 |
But [<s>Brahman</s>] is more [than <s>Prakṛti</s>], because of the scriptural indication of difference. | BBs 2.1.22 |
And like stones etc., that [objection] is untenable. | BBs 2.1.23 |

body.text: upasaṃhāradarśanān neti cen na kṣīravad dhi | BBs_2,1.24 |
body.translated_text: If [one says] not so, because withdrawal [of the world into its cause] is observed — no, because it is like milk [transforming into curds]. | BBs 2.1.24 |
And as with <s>devas</s> and others in the world. | BBs 2.1.25 |
Either the entire [<s>Brahman</s>] would be involved [in transformation], or there would be a contradiction with the word 'partless.' | BBs 2.1.26 |
But [it is established] from scripture (<s>śruti</s>), because [the Vedānta doctrine] has scripture as its foundation. | BBs 2.1.27 |

body.text: ātmani caivaṃ vicitrāś ca hi | BBs_2,1.28 |
body.translated_text: And in the Self itself, [manifold creation is possible] because [powers] are indeed manifold. | BBs 2.1.28 |
And because of the defect in [the objector's] own position. | BBs 2.1.29 |
And [<s>Brahman</s>] is endowed with all [powers], as this is seen [in scripture]. | BBs 2.1.30 |

body.text: vikaraṇatvān neti cet tad uktam | BBs_2,1.31 |
body.translated_text: If [one objects that <s>Brahman</s>] is without instruments [of creation] — that has [already] been answered. | BBs 2.1.31 |
[Creation is] not [purposeless], because it has a purpose. | BBs 2.1.32 |
But [creation is] mere sport (<s>līlā</s>), as in the world. | BBs 2.1.33 |

body.text: vaiṣamyanairghṛṇye na sāpekṣatvāt tathā hi darśayati | BBs_2,1.34 |
body.translated_text: [The charge of] partiality and cruelty [against God] does not [apply], because [creation] is dependent [on the <s>karma</s> of beings]; for thus [scripture] shows. | BBs 2.1.34 |

body.text: na karmāvibhāgād iti cen nānāditvād upapadyate cāpy upalabhyate ca | BBs_2,1.35 |
body.translated_text: If [one says] not, because of the non-distinction of <s>karma</s> [before the first creation] — no, because [<s>karma</s>] is beginningless; and it is established and also observed [to be so]. | BBs 2.1.35 |
And because all attributes [of <s>Brahman</s>] are established [by scripture]. | BBs 2.1.36 |

body.text: racanānupapatteś ca nānumānaṃ pravṛtteś ca | BBs_2,2.1 |
body.translated_text: Because the design [of the world] cannot be explained [by <s>Pradhāna</s>], inference [alone is insufficient]; and because of activity [requiring consciousness]. | BBs 2.2.1 |
If [one says it is] like milk and water — even there [a conscious agent is required]. | BBs 2.2.2 |
And because the separation [of <s>Puruṣa</s> from <s>Prakṛti</s>] has no stable basis, and because [<s>Pradhāna</s>] is independent [of any conscious agent]. | BBs 2.2.3 |
And because [purposeful design] is absent elsewhere [in unconscious matter] — not like grass and the like. | BBs 2.2.4 |
If [one says it is] like a person and a magnet — even so [the objection applies]. | BBs 2.2.5 |
And because the [<s>Pradhāna</s>'s] being a component [of the body] is untenable. | BBs 2.2.6 |
And because, in the alternative inference, there would be a separation from the capacity of the knower. | BBs 2.2.7 |
Even if [the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position] is accepted, [there would be] absence of purpose. | BBs 2.2.8 |
And because of contradictions, [the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine] is untenable. | BBs 2.2.9 |
[The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> atoms would have to be] large and long, or [they would have to be] small and spherical [— either way there is a defect]. | BBs 2.2.10 |
In either case, [the atoms cannot produce] action; hence there is absence [of creation]. | BBs 2.2.11 |
And because of the acceptance of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), there is an infinite regress due to parity [of reasoning]. | BBs 2.2.12 |
And because [atoms] would be eternally [combined or separated]. | BBs 2.2.13 |
And because [atoms] possess form etc., the reverse [i.e., their being eternal] is observed [to be untenable]. | BBs 2.2.14 |
And because there are defects in either case. | BBs 2.2.15 |
Because [the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system] is not accepted [by the learned], there is complete disregard [for it]. | BBs 2.2.16 |
Even if [the aggregate has] both kinds of causes, that [creation] is not attained. | BBs 2.2.17 |

body.text: itaretarapratyayatvād upapannam iti cen na saṅghātabhāvānimittatvāt | BBs_2,2.18 |
body.translated_text: If [one says the Buddhist doctrine] is established because of mutual causation — no, because the aggregate does not arise without a cause. | BBs 2.2.18 |
And because, when the later [moment] arises, the earlier ceases. | BBs 2.2.19 |
Without [a permanent self], the thesis [of Buddhism] would be contradicted; [and] there would be simultaneity, or else [absurdity]. | BBs 2.2.20 |
Neither analytical nor non-analytical cessation is attained, because of the unbroken [flow of consciousness]. | BBs 2.2.21 |
And because there are defects in either case [of the Buddhist view]. | BBs 2.2.22 |
And in [the case of] space, because of no distinction [between the Buddhist schools]. | BBs 2.2.23 |
And because of memory [which requires a permanent self]. | BBs 2.2.24 |
[The world does] not [arise] from non-existence, because [such arising] is not observed. | BBs 2.2.25 |
Even for the indifferent [Buddhist schools], establishment [of their position] would be the same [i.e., impossible]. | BBs 2.2.26 |
[External objects are] not non-existent, because [they are] apprehended. | BBs 2.2.27 |
And because of the difference [between waking and dream], [the world] is not like dreams etc. | BBs 2.2.28 |
[External objects] do not exist [as mere consciousness], because [they are] not apprehended [as such]. | BBs 2.2.29 |
And because [the <s>Vijñānavāda</s> is] altogether untenable. | BBs 2.2.30 |
[Consciousness does] not [reside] in a single [entity], because of the impossibility. | BBs 2.2.31 |
And thus [there would be] incompleteness of the Self. | BBs 2.2.32 |

body.text: na ca paryāyād apy avirodho vikārādibhyaḥ | BBs_2,2.33 |
body.translated_text: And not even by alternation [of states] is there non-contradiction, because of transformation and other [difficulties]. | BBs 2.2.33 |
And because both [the <s>Jaina</s> predicates] are eternal, [and both are associated] with the final state, there is no distinction. | BBs 2.2.34 |
Because of the incoherence of the Lord [in the <s>Jaina</s> system]. | BBs 2.2.35 |
And because [the <s>Jaina</s> view of] substratum is untenable. | BBs 2.2.36 |
If [the self is said to be] like an instrument — no, because of experience etc. | BBs 2.2.37 |
[The Lord would be] either finite or not omniscient. | BBs 2.2.38 |
Because origination [of the world from atoms] is impossible. | BBs 2.2.39 |
And the agent is not [identical with] the instrument. | BBs 2.2.40 |
Or, if [things] consist of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) etc., even then that [view] is not refuted. | BBs 2.2.41 |
And because of contradictions [in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> or <s>Bhāgavata</s> doctrine]. | BBs 2.2.42 |
Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is not [created], because there is no scriptural statement [of its creation]. | BBs 2.3.1 |
But it does [exist as created]. | BBs 2.3.2 |
Because [the non-creation interpretation] cannot be metaphorical, and because of [explicit] scripture. | BBs 2.3.3 |
And it is possible [that ākāśa refers to <s>Brahman</s>] in one [passage], as with the word '<s>Brahman</s>.' | BBs 2.3.4 |
[Otherwise] the thesis [that all originates from <s>Brahman</s>] would be abandoned, because of non-difference [between ākāśa and <s>Brahman</s>]. | BBs 2.3.5 |
From the [scriptural] words. | BBs 2.3.6 |
But the differentiation [of elements extends only] as far as [their] modification, as in the world. | BBs 2.3.7 |
By this, <s>Mātariśvan</s> (Air) is explained. | BBs 2.3.8 |
But [the origination of the Self] is impossible, because of the impossibility [of something originating] from what already exists. | BBs 2.3.9 |
Fire [is created] after that [air], for thus [scripture] says. | BBs 2.3.10 |
Water. | BBs 2.3.11 |
Earth. | BBs 2.3.12 |
From the context, the form [mentioned in scripture], and other words. | BBs 2.3.13 |

body.text: tadabhidhyānād eva tu talliṅgāt saḥ | BBs_2,3.14 |
body.translated_text: But because of His meditation [upon those elements], and because of the indicatory marks, He [the individual self is also created]. | BBs 2.3.14 |

body.text: viparyayeṇa tu kramo 'ta upapadyate ca | BBs_2,3.15 |
body.translated_text: But the reverse order [of dissolution is established], and this is also reasonable. | BBs 2.3.15 |

body.text: antarā vijñānamanasī krameṇa talliṅgād iti cen nāviśeṣāt | BBs_2,3.16 |
body.translated_text: If [one says that] consciousness and mind [are created] in between, in sequence, because of indicatory marks — no, because of non-distinction [between them]. | BBs 2.3.16 |

body.text: carācaravyapāśrayas tu syāt tadvyapadeśo bhāktas tadbhāvabhāvitvāt | BBs_2,3.17 |
body.translated_text: But [the statement about] dependence on the movable and immovable should [be understood as] a figurative designation [of <s>Brahman</s>], because [creation] arises from its being. | BBs 2.3.17 |

body.text: nātmā śruter nityatvāc ca tābhyaḥ | BBs_2,3.18 |
body.translated_text: The Self (<s>Ātman</s>) [is] not [created], because of scripture and because of its eternality according to those [scriptural passages]. | BBs 2.3.18 |
[The Self is] a knower, for the same reason. | BBs 2.3.19 |
[This is known] from departure, going, and return. | BBs 2.3.20 |
And by its own self, in the two latter [i.e., going and return]. | BBs 2.3.21 |
If [one says the self is] not atomic, because scripture does not [teach so] — no, because [that passage refers to] the other [i.e., the Supreme Self], who is the [main] topic. | BBs 2.3.22 |
And from its own designation [as atomic] and from [scriptural] measure. | BBs 2.3.23 |
There is no contradiction, as with sandal-paste [which, though applied to one spot, cools the whole body]. | BBs 2.3.24 |

body.text: avasthitivaiśeṣyād iti cen nābhyupagamād dhṛdi hi | BBs_2,3.25 |
body.translated_text: If [one says] because of the difference in location [the self cannot pervade the body] — no, because of the accepted [teaching] that [the self dwells] in the heart. | BBs 2.3.25 |
Or because of [its pervasive] quality, as in the world. | BBs 2.3.26 |

body.text: vyatireko gandhavat tathā hi darśayati | BBs_2,3.27 |
body.translated_text: The separateness [of the self from the body is] like fragrance [from the flower]; for thus [scripture] shows. | BBs 2.3.27 |
Because of the separate teaching [of self and body]. | BBs 2.3.28 |
But [the self is] designated [by the term 'intelligence'] because intelligence is its essential quality — like the Supreme Knower (<s>Prājña</s>). | BBs 2.3.29 |

body.text: yāvadātmabhāvitvāc ca na doṣas taddarśanāt | BBs_2,3.30 |
body.translated_text: And there is no fault, because [intelligence] lasts as long as the self lasts; for that is shown [in scripture]. | BBs 2.3.30 |
But like masculinity etc., [the self's agency] is through the manifestation of what already exists. | BBs 2.3.31 |
[Otherwise] there would be the consequence of eternal perception or eternal non-perception, or a restriction to one or the other [state]. | BBs 2.3.32 |
[The self] is an agent, because [otherwise] scripture would be purposeless. | BBs 2.3.33 |
And because of the teaching about undertaking and cessation [of action]. | BBs 2.3.34 |

body.text: vyapadeśāc ca kriyāyāṃ na cen nirdeśaviparyayaḥ | BBs_2,3.35 |
body.translated_text: And because of the designation in connection with action — [and] if [one says] not, [then] the statement would be reversed. | BBs 2.3.35 |
As with perception, there is no fixed rule [about the self's agency]. | BBs 2.3.36 |
Because of the reversal of powers [in different states]. | BBs 2.3.37 |
And because of the absence [of agency] in <s>samādhi</s>. | BBs 2.3.38 |
And as with a carpenter, [the self acts] in both ways. | BBs 2.3.39 |
But from the Supreme [the self's agency derives], because thus scripture declares. | BBs 2.3.40 |
But [the Supreme Self] has regard for the effort made [by the individual self], because of the non-purposelessness of injunctions and prohibitions, and other [reasons]. | BBs 2.3.41 |

body.text: aṃśo nānāvyapadeśād anyathā cāpi dāśakitavāditvam adhīyata eke | BBs_2,3.42 |
body.translated_text: [The individual self is] a part [of <s>Brahman</s>], because of the manifold designations [in scripture]; otherwise, there would also be [the objection of <s>Brahman</s> being] like a fisherman or a gambler — for some [Vedic schools] recite thus. | BBs 2.3.42 |
From the letters of the <s>mantra</s> [this is confirmed]. | BBs 2.3.43 |
It is also remembered [in <s>smṛti</s> texts]. | BBs 2.3.44 |
But like light etc., the Supreme is not so [limited by being a whole of parts]. | BBs 2.3.45 |
And they remember [this in <s>smṛti</s>]. | BBs 2.3.46 |
Permission and prohibition [are possible] because of the connection with a body — like light and the like. | BBs 2.3.47 |
And because of non-continuity [of bodies], there is no intermixture [of results]. | BBs 2.3.48 |
And [the individual self is] merely a reflection. | BBs 2.3.49 |
Because of the non-restriction of the unseen [<s>adṛṣṭa</s>]. | BBs 2.3.50 |
And thus also with regard to intention and the like. | BBs 2.3.51 |
If [one says the difference is] due to difference of location — no, because of [the self's] being within [<s>Brahman</s>]. | BBs 2.3.52 |
Likewise the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) [are created by <s>Brahman</s>]. | BBs 2.4.1 |
Because a metaphorical [interpretation] is not possible, and because of the prior scriptural statement. | BBs 2.4.2 |
Speech is preceded by that [<s>prāṇa</s>]. | BBs 2.4.3 |
[The <s>prāṇas</s> are] seven, because of their movement and [scriptural] specification. | BBs 2.4.4 |
But the hands and others [are not prāṇas in the primary sense], because they abide [in the body even in deep sleep]; hence [they are] not so. | BBs 2.4.5 |
And [the prāṇas] are minute. | BBs 2.4.6 |
And the chief [<s>prāṇa</s> is also created]. | BBs 2.4.7 |
[The chief <s>prāṇa</s>] is not [merely] air or a function [of air], because of the separate teaching. | BBs 2.4.8 |
But like the eye and others, [the chief <s>prāṇa</s> is a sense organ,] because of its being taught together [with them] and other [reasons]. | BBs 2.4.9 |

body.text: akaraṇatvāc ca na doṣas tathā hi darśayati | BBs_2,4.10 |
body.translated_text: And because [the chief <s>prāṇa</s>] is not an instrument [of specific knowledge], there is no fault; for thus [scripture] shows. | BBs 2.4.10 |
[The chief <s>prāṇa</s>] has five functions and is designated like the mind. | BBs 2.4.11 |
And (the individual soul is) atomic (in size). (BSū 2.4.12)

body.text: jyotir ādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ tu tadāmananātprāṇavatā śabdāt | BBs_2,4.13 |
body.translated_text: But (the soul has) light and other (qualities) as its substratum, because of the statement that it is endowed with <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath), from the scriptural word. (BSū 2.4.13)
And because of its (the soul's) permanence. (BSū 2.4.14)

body.text: ta indriyāṇi tadvyapadeśād anyatra śreṣṭhāt | BBs_2,4.15 |
body.translated_text: These are the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), because they are so designated, except for the chief one (<s>Prāṇa</s>). (BSū 2.4.15)
Because of the scriptural declaration of difference, and because of their distinct characteristics. (BSū 2.4.16)
But the creation of names and forms is by the one who performs the tripartite making, as taught by scripture. (BSū 2.4.17)
Flesh and the like are products of earth, as stated by scripture; and similarly for the other two (elements). (BSū 2.4.18)
But the designation as that (particular element) is because of predominance; the designation as that is because of predominance. (BSū 2.4.19)
When the soul obtains its next (body), it departs enveloped (by the subtle elements), as established by questions and explanations (in scripture). (BSū 3.1.1)
But (the soul departs) with the threefold constitution (of the elements), on account of the preponderance (of any one element being due to the mixture). (BSū 3.1.2)
And because of the departure of <s>Prāṇa</s> (being mentioned in scripture). (BSū 3.1.3)

body.text: agnyādiśruter iti cen na bhāktatvāt | BBs_3,1.4 |
body.translated_text: If it be said (that the soul goes to) fire and so on, on account of scriptural statement, (we say) no, because (the statement is) figurative. (BSū 3.1.4)

body.text: prathame 'śravaṇād iti cen na tā eva hy upapatteḥ | BBs_3,1.5 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that (the soul is) not mentioned in the first (oblation), (we say) no, for those (fires) are indeed appropriate. (BSū 3.1.5)

body.text: aśrutatvād iti cen neṣṭādikāriṇāṃ pratīteḥ | BBs_3,1.6 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that (the five-fire doctrine) is not heard (in all recensions), (we say) no, because it is understood for those who have performed <s>iṣṭa</s> (sacrifices) and the like. (BSū 3.1.6)

body.text: bhāktaṃ vānātmavittvāt tathā hi darśayati | BBs_3,1.7 |
body.translated_text: Or (the going to fire etc. is) figurative, because (the soul described is) not a knower of the Self; for thus (the scripture) shows. (BSū 3.1.7)
Upon the exhaustion of (good) works, (the soul) descends with a residue (of <s>karma</s>), as seen from scripture and <s>smṛti</s>; in the same manner (as it went up), and not otherwise. (BSū 3.1.8)

body.text: caraṇād iti cen na tadupalakṣaṇārtheti kārṣṇājiniḥ | BBs_3,1.9 |
body.translated_text: If it be said (that the descent is) because of conduct (<s>caraṇa</s>), (we say) no, for that (word) is meant as an indication (of <s>karma</s>); thus (says) <s>Kārṣṇājini</s>. (BSū 3.1.9)

body.text: ānarthakyam iti cen na tadapekṣatvāt | BBs_3,1.10 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that (good conduct) would be purposeless (if it merely indicates <s>karma</s>), (we say) no, because (good conduct) is dependent on that (<s>karma</s>). (BSū 3.1.10)
But (the term <s>caraṇa</s> means) good and evil works only; thus (says) <s>Bādari</s>. (BSū 3.1.11)
And for those who perform neither <s>iṣṭa</s> nor forbidden acts, it is also stated in scripture. (BSū 3.1.12)

body.text: saṃyamane tv anubhūyetareṣāmārohāv arohau tadgatidarśanāt | BBs_3,1.13 |
body.translated_text: But in the abode of <s>Yama</s>, having experienced (the results), for the others (who are sinful) there is ascent and descent, as that path is shown (in scripture). (BSū 3.1.13)
And the <s>smṛtis</s> (also) state (this). (BSū 3.1.14)
(There are) also seven (hells, according to some texts). (BSū 3.1.15)
Even there, there is no contradiction, because of the operation of that (same principle of karmic retribution). (BSū 3.1.16)
But (the two paths are) for (those who have) knowledge and works, because that is the subject under discussion. (BSū 3.1.17)
(There is) not (such a path) in the third (case, i.e., for the wicked), as is observed (from scripture). (BSū 3.1.18)
And it is remembered also in the world (that the wicked have no such path). (BSū 3.1.19)
And because (scripture) shows (this). (BSū 3.1.20)
The inclusion of the third term (<s>saṃśokaja</s>, born of grief/mixture) is (for those born from moisture and the like). (BSū 3.1.21)
The attainment of that nature (of the respective species) is reasonable. (BSū 3.1.22)
Not after a very long time, because of the specific (statement in scripture). (BSū 3.1.23)
(When the soul) enters another (body) presided over (by another soul), it is as before, because of the scriptural declaration. (BSū 3.1.24)

body.text: aśuddham iti cen na śabdāt | BBs_3,1.25 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that (the soul becomes) impure (by contact with the body), (we say) no, on account of the scriptural word (to the contrary). (BSū 3.1.25)
Then (there is) the union with the seminal fluid. (BSū 3.1.26)
From the womb, the body (is produced). (BSū 3.1.27)
In the intermediate state (of dream), (there is) creation (by the soul); for (the scripture) says so. (BSū 3.2.1)
And some (teach that the Lord is) the creator (of dreams); and (in dreams appear) sons and other (things). (BSū 3.2.2)
But (dream is) mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion), because the (soul's) nature is not fully manifested (in dream). (BSū 3.2.3)

body.text: parābhidhyānāt tu tirohitaṃ tato hyasya bandhaviparyayau | BBs_3,2.4 |
body.translated_text: But (the dream creation is) concealed through the meditation of the Supreme; for from that (Supreme) arise the soul's bondage and its opposite (liberation). (BSū 3.2.4)
Or that (concealment) also (occurs) because of connection with the body. (BSū 3.2.5)

body.text: sūcakaś ca hi śruterācakṣate ca tadvidaḥ | BBs_3,2.6 |
body.translated_text: And (dreams are) indicative (of future events), for scripture declares (this), and the knowers of that (science of dreams) also state (this). (BSū 3.2.6)
The absence of that (dream state occurs) in the <s>nāḍīs</s> (nerves, during deep sleep), as stated in scripture, and (the soul rests) in the Self. (BSū 3.2.7)
Therefore, awakening is from that (Brahman, with which the soul was united in deep sleep). (BSū 3.2.8)
But it is the same (soul that awakes), because of (the scriptural statements about) <s>karma</s>, memory, scriptural text, and injunction. (BSū 3.2.9)
The state of swoon is a half-attainment (of death), by the method of elimination. (BSū 3.2.10)

body.text: na sthānato 'pi parasyobhayaliṅgaṃ sarvatra hi | BBs_3,2.11 |
body.translated_text: Not even from (any particular) place does the Supreme (Brahman have) both characteristics (form and formlessness); for everywhere (scripture declares both). (BSū 3.2.11)

body.text: bhedād iti cen na pratyekamatadvacanāt | BBs_3,2.12 |
body.translated_text: If it be said (that there is contradiction) because of difference, (we say) no, because each (text) negates (the other attribute), not both at once. (BSū 3.2.12)
And thus some (scriptures) indeed (declare). (BSū 3.2.13)
(Brahman is) indeed formless, for that (formlessness) is its principal nature. (BSū 3.2.14)
And like light, (the attribution of form is) not purposeless. (BSū 3.2.15)
(Scripture) also says that (Brahman is) only that (pure being, without form). (BSū 3.2.16)
(Scripture) shows (this); and moreover, (the <s>smṛtis</s>) also remember (this). (BSū 3.2.17)
For this very reason, the comparison (of Brahman) is like the sun and similar (things, whose reflections appear manifold). (BSū 3.2.18)
But (Brahman is) not like water (which actually undergoes change); because of the non-apprehension (of any real change in Brahman), such is not the case. (BSū 3.2.19)

(Brahman does not partake of) increase and decrease, because (the individual souls are) included (within Brahman); and because of the consistency of both (sets of scriptural texts); and because (scripture) shows (this). (BSū 3.2.20)

body.text: prakṛtaitāvattvaṃ hi pratiṣedhati tato bravīti ca bhūyaḥ | BBs_3,2.21 |
body.translated_text: (Scripture) indeed negates (Brahman being) only so much as described; then it speaks of (Brahman as being) more (than any description). (BSū 3.2.21)
That (Brahman) is unmanifest, for (scripture) says so. (BSū 3.2.22)
Moreover, through devoted worship, (Brahman is realized) by direct perception and inference. (BSū 3.2.23)
And as (Brahman is) like light, there is no distinction; and light (manifests) in action, through repeated practice. (BSū 3.2.24)
Therefore (Brahman is described) as infinite; for thus is the indicatory mark (in scripture). (BSū 3.2.25)
But because of the twofold designation (as possessing and not possessing qualities), (the relation is) like that of a serpent and its coils (i.e., identity with distinction). (BSū 3.2.26)
Or like (the relation of) light and its source, because of (Brahman's) luminous nature. (BSū 3.2.27)
Or as stated before (the relation between Brahman and the world is to be understood as previously explained). (BSū 3.2.28)
And because of the (scriptural) negation (of all distinctions from Brahman). (BSū 3.2.29)
From the Supreme, (the descriptions of) bridge, measure, connection, and difference are designations (for the purpose of meditation). (BSū 3.2.30)
But (these are) on account of similarity (of the meditation contexts, not actual difference in Brahman). (BSū 3.2.31)
(The descriptions are) for the sake of intellectual comprehension, like (the description of Brahman having) feet. (BSū 3.2.32)
(The difference in result is) because of the difference in the special place (of meditation), as in the case of light and similar (things). (BSū 3.2.33)
And because it is reasonable. (BSū 3.2.34)
And because of the negation of the other (view, i.e., that Brahman is limited). (BSū 3.2.35)
By this (the <s>sūtras</s> establish) the all-pervadingness (of Brahman), from the terms denoting extent and similar (expressions in scripture). (BSū 3.2.36)
The fruit (of meditation comes) from that (Brahman), because it is reasonable. (BSū 3.2.37)
And because it is so declared in scripture. (BSū 3.2.38)
<s>Jaimini</s> (holds that) <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct is the means of attaining results), for that very reason. (BSū 3.2.39)
But <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> (holds that) the former (i.e., Brahman is the bestower of fruits), because (Brahman) is designated as the cause. (BSū 3.2.40)
The knowledge (of Brahman taught) in all <s>Vedānta</s> texts (is one), because there is no difference in the injunction and other (aspects). (BSū 3.3.1)

body.text: bhedān neti ced ekasyām api | BBs_3,3.2 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that (the <s>vidyās</s> are) not (one) because of differences, (we say) no, for (such differences exist) even within a single (recension). (BSū 3.3.2)

body.text: svādhyāyasya tathātve hi samācāre 'dhikārāc ca savavac ca tanniyamaḥ | BBs_3,3.3 |
body.translated_text: Since the own-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is such (i.e., one despite recension differences), because of the practice, eligibility, and because the restriction is like that of the <s>Sava</s> sacrifice; this has been stated. (BSū 3.3.3)
And (scripture) shows (this unity of <s>vidyās</s>). (BSū 3.3.4)

The combination (of particulars from different texts of the same <s>vidyā</s> is proper) because there is no difference in the object (of meditation), as in the case of subsidiary injunctions; and because (the <s>vidyās</s>) are the same. (BSū 3.3.5)

body.text: anyathātvaṃ śabdād iti cen nāviśeṣāt | BBs_3,3.6 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that (the <s>vidyās</s> are) different because of (difference in) wording, (we say) no, because there is no (real) difference. (BSū 3.3.6)
Or (they are) not (to be combined), because of the difference in context, as in the case of (the meditation on Brahman as) the highest and the great. (BSū 3.3.7)

body.text: saṃjñātaś cet tad uktam asti tu tad api | BBs_3,3.8 |
body.translated_text: If (the objection is raised) because of the name (being the same, they must be one), that has been answered; but that (distinction based on context) also exists. (BSū 3.3.8)
And because of the comprehensive applicability (of this principle), it is harmonious. (BSū 3.3.9)
Because of the non-difference of everything (taught in the <s>Upaniṣads</s> about Brahman), these other (attributes mentioned in various texts) are (to be combined). (BSū 3.3.10)
Bliss and other (attributes belong to) the principal (Brahman, and are to be included in all meditations on Brahman). (BSū 3.3.11)

(The objection that attributes like) 'having joy as the head' and so on would not be obtained (in other <s>vidyās</s> is answered by saying that) increase and decrease (of attributes occur only) when there is difference (of <s>vidyā</s>). (BSū 3.3.12)
But the others (i.e., attributes like bliss etc. are to be combined) because of the similarity of purport. (BSū 3.3.13)
(Attributes like bliss are not merely) for the sake of meditation (in one <s>vidyā</s> alone), because there would be no purpose (in their separate mention otherwise). (BSū 3.3.14)
And because of the word '<s>Ātman</s>' (being used, which shows these are essential attributes of Brahman itself). (BSū 3.3.15)
The apprehension of (Brahman as) the Self is (to be adopted) from the later (texts) as in other (cases). (BSū 3.3.16)

body.text: anvayād iti cet syād avadhāraṇāt | BBs_3,3.17 |
body.translated_text: If it be said (that the attributes belong to the meditation) because of the connected sequence, (we say) it would be so (only if there were no) definite ascertainment (otherwise). (BSū 3.3.17)
Because it describes something to be accomplished (<s>kārya</s>), it is a new (injunction, not a mere repetition). (BSū 3.3.18)
(The meditation is) the same in this way, and because of non-difference (of the object meditated upon). (BSū 3.3.19)
Because of the connection (of the same meditation), it is likewise in other (recensions) also. (BSū 3.3.20)
Or not (to be combined), because of the specific difference (in the details of the meditation). (BSū 3.3.21)
And (scripture) shows (this). (BSū 3.3.22)
Moreover, on account of (the difference in) assembling (of materials), the abode (being heaven), and the extent, also from this (it follows that the meditations are different). (BSū 3.3.23)
In the <s>Puruṣavidyā</s> also, (the attributes of the other recensions are not to be combined) because the others are not mentioned (there). (BSū 3.3.24)
Because of the difference in purpose, such as piercing (the sun's disc) and so on. (BSū 3.3.25)

In the case of (those details which may be) omitted, (they are merely) complementary to the word of the <s>Upaniṣad</s> (not essential), like <s>kuśa</s> grass, metres, hymns of praise, and recitation; this has been stated. (BSū 3.3.26)

body.text: sāṃparāye tartavyābhāvāt tathā hy anye | BBs_3,3.27 |
body.translated_text: At the time of death (on the journey of the soul), there is nothing to be attained (by those meditations, for those on the path of the gods); for thus other (scriptural texts declare). (BSū 3.3.27)
(The meditations may be performed) at will, because there is no conflict with either (view). (BSū 3.3.28)

body.text: gater arthavattvam ubhayathānyathā hi virodhaḥ | BBs_3,3.29 |
body.translated_text: The journey (of the soul along the path of the gods) has a purpose in both ways (whether the meditations include the details or not); for otherwise there would be contradiction. (BSū 3.3.29)
(The view that the journey has purpose) is established, because the marks indicating that meaning are found, as in the world. (BSū 3.3.30)
(The meditations) remain valid as long as the eligibility (for them lasts), for those who are entitled to (particular) meditations. (BSū 3.3.31)
There is no fixed rule (restricting a meditation to particular <s>āśramas</s>) for all (meditations), and there is no contradiction, from scripture and reasoning. (BSū 3.3.32)

But for the meditations on the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>), there is inclusion (of common attributes), because of commonality and the existence of that (same Brahman as the object); as in the case of the <s>Upasad</s> offerings; this has been stated. (BSū 3.3.33)
Because only so much (is taught in each <s>vidyā</s>, the particulars of each are not to be combined with others). (BSū 3.3.34)

body.text: antarā bhūtagrāmavatsvātmano 'nyathā bhedānupapattir iti cen nopadeśavat | BBs_3,3.35 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that (Brahman) being within (the individual soul) like a group of elements, and being different from the Self, the difference cannot be maintained — (we say) no, because (the teaching is) like an instruction (using familiar illustrations). (BSū 3.3.35)
The interchange (of attributes is proper, for the scriptures) distinguish (them) thus, as in other (cases). (BSū 3.3.36)
That (Brahman described in different <s>vidyās</s>) is indeed the same, (being characterized by) truth and other (attributes). (BSū 3.3.37)
(Attributes such as) desire and others (mentioned) in one place (are to be included) in the other (meditation) also, because of (identity of) the abode and other (reasons). (BSū 3.3.38)
Because of the respect (shown to the meditation in scripture), there is no omission (of any detail). (BSū 3.3.39)
When (the qualification for meditation) is present, (the meditation is to be performed) then, because of the scriptural statement to that effect. (BSū 3.3.40)

There is no fixed rule as to the determination of that (particular meditation to be practiced), because that (freedom of choice) is observed (in scripture); for separately (each meditation) has no obstruction (and bears) fruit. (BSū 3.3.41)
(The combining of attributes is) just like a gift (<s>pradāna</s>); this has been stated. (BSū 3.3.42)
Because of the preponderance of indicatory marks (<s>liṅga</s>), that indeed is stronger; and that (principle) also (applies here). (BSū 3.3.43)
The option stated earlier (applies) because of the context; it would be like a (subsidiary) act being performed (in a sacrifice). (BSū 3.3.44)
And because of the extended application (<s>atideśa</s>, the same principle holds). (BSū 3.3.45)
But (the determining factor is) the <s>vidyā</s> alone, because of the conclusive determination, and because (scripture) shows (this). (BSū 3.3.46)
And there is no sublation (of the <s>vidyā</s>), because of the greater strength of scripture and other (means of knowledge). (BSū 3.3.47)
Because of the connection and other (reasons), (each <s>vidyā</s> is) separate from other meditations, as is observed; and this has been stated. (BSū 3.3.48)

Not even from a general (similarity of attributes can the <s>vidyās</s> be combined), because of the (different) results perceived, as in the case of death (being the result of certain rites); for there is no worldly convergence (of different rites with different results). (BSū 3.3.49)

body.text: pareṇa ca śabdasya tādvidhyaṃ bhūyastvāt tv anubandhaḥ | BBs_3,3.50 |
body.translated_text: And the word (used in different contexts) has that (same) character because of (its connection with) the Supreme; but the connection (of attributes is based) on the preponderance (of common features). (BSū 3.3.50)
(There is) one (meditation on the Self) because of the existence (of the Self) in the body. (BSū 3.3.51)
The separation (of the meditation from bodily existence) is because it exists wherever that (Self) exists; but not like (mere) perception (which depends on the senses). (BSū 3.3.52)

body.text: aṅgāvabaddhāstu na śākhāsu hi prativedam | BBs_3,3.53 |
body.translated_text: But those (details) which are parts (of a sacrifice) are restricted (to their own branches) and are not (to be combined) across the <s>śākhās</s> (Vedic branches), for (they are prescribed) in each Veda (separately). (BSū 3.3.53)
Or (there is) no contradiction, as in the case of <s>mantras</s> and the like (which are used across branches). (BSū 3.3.54)

body.text: bhūmnaḥ kratuvajjyāyasvaṃ tathā hi darśayati | BBs_3,3.55 |
body.translated_text: The meditation on the <s>Bhūman</s> (the Infinite) is superior, like a sacrifice, for thus the scripture shows. (BBs 3.3.55)
They are different, because of the difference in words and other factors. (BBs 3.3.56)
There is an option, since the results are not different. (BBs 3.3.57)

body.text: kāmyāstu yathākāmaṃ samuccīyeranna vā pūrvahetvabhāvāt | BBs_3,3.58 |
body.translated_text: But those that are desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>) may or may not be combined as one wishes, because the previous reason does not apply. (BBs 3.3.58)
With regard to the subsidiary elements (<s>aṅgas</s>), they belong to their respective bases as appropriate. (BBs 3.3.59)
And because of scriptural instruction. (BBs 3.3.60)
Because of the aggregation. (BBs 3.3.61)
And because of the scripture declaring the qualities to be common. (BBs 3.3.62)
Or not, because there is no scriptural statement of their co-existence. (BBs 3.3.63)
And because it is seen (in scripture). (BBs 3.3.64)
The purpose of man (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) is from this, because of the scriptural word — thus says <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>. (BBs 3.4.1)
Because of being subsidiary, the statements about the purpose of man are <s>arthavāda</s> (glorificatory passages), as in other cases — thus says <s>Jaimini</s>. (BBs 3.4.2)
Because of the observation of conduct (of the knowers). (BBs 3.4.3)
Because scripture states so. (BBs 3.4.4)
Because of the commencement together (of knowledge and works). (BBs 3.4.5)
Because there is injunction for one who possesses that (knowledge). (BBs 3.4.6)
Because of the rule (restricting to those qualified). (BBs 3.4.7)
But <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>'s view prevails because of the additional teaching, for thus it is seen (in scripture). (BBs 3.4.8)
But the observation (of conduct) is equal (on both sides). (BBs 3.4.9)
It is not universal. (BBs 3.4.10)
The division is like that of the hundredfold (offering). (BBs 3.4.11)
For one who merely studies (the Veda). (BBs 3.4.12)
Not so, because there is no distinction. (BBs 3.4.13)
Or it is a permission for the sake of praise. (BBs 3.4.14)
And some (teach) according to one's own will. (BBs 3.4.15)
And the violation (of duties would follow). (BBs 3.4.16)
And among the <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> (celibate ascetics), for the word (of scripture supports this). (BBs 3.4.17)
<s>Jaimini</s> refutes the reference (to renunciation) because of the injunction (of rites), for (scripture) indeed negates it. (BBs 3.4.18)
It is to be observed — so says <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> — because of the scriptural statement of equality. (BBs 3.4.19)
Or it is an injunction, like the holding (of a sacrificial implement). (BBs 3.4.20)

body.text: stutimātram upādānād iti cen nāpūrvatvāt | BBs_3,4.21 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that it is mere praise, because of the reference (to something already known), no, because of its novelty. (BBs 3.4.21)
And because of the word expressing being (existence, not mere praise). (BBs 3.4.22)

body.text: pāriplavārthā iti cen na viśeṣitatvāt | BBs_3,4.23 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that they serve the purpose of the <s>pāriplava</s> (recitation cycle), no, because they are specifically characterized. (BBs 3.4.23)
And also because of their connection in a single passage. (BBs 3.4.24)
For this very reason there is no dependence on the fire-kindling and other (preliminary rites). (BBs 3.4.25)
And there is dependence on all (requisites), because of the scriptural statement of sacrifice and the like, as in the case of the horse (sacrifice). (BBs 3.4.26)

body.text: śamadamādyupetas syāt tathāpi tu tadvidhes tadaṅgatayā teṣām apy avaśyānuṣṭheyatvāt | BBs_3,4.27 |
body.translated_text: One should be endowed with <s>śama</s> (tranquility), <s>dama</s> (self-control), and the rest; yet even so, those are enjoined as auxiliaries to that (knowledge), since they must necessarily be practiced. (BBs 3.4.27)

body.text: sarvān nānumatiś ca prāṇātyaye taddarśanāt | BBs_3,4.28 |
body.translated_text: And the permission for all (foods) is only when life is in danger, for thus it is seen (in scripture). (BBs 3.4.28)
And because there is no contradiction (with scriptural rules). (BBs 3.4.29)
It is also stated in <s>Smṛti</s>. (BBs 3.4.30)
And the scriptural word (indicates that one should) not act according to mere whim. (BBs 3.4.31)
And the duties of the <s>āśrama</s> (stages of life) also, because they are enjoined. (BBs 3.4.32)
And as being auxiliary (to knowledge). (BBs 3.4.33)
In all cases, they (the duties) are the same, because of the twofold indicatory marks. (BBs 3.4.34)
And scripture shows that (knowledge) is not overcome (by evil deeds). (BBs 3.4.35)
But even in between (i.e., in intermediate stages of life), because that is seen (in scripture). (BBs 3.4.36)
It is also stated in <s>Smṛti</s>. (BBs 3.4.37)
And there is special grace (for such seekers). (BBs 3.4.38)

body.text: atas tv itarajjyāyo liṅgāc ca | BBs_3,4.39 |
body.translated_text: Therefore, however, the other (the life of renunciation) is better, because of the indicatory marks. (BBs 3.4.39)

body.text: tadbhūtasya tu nātadbhāvo jaiminer api niyamāt tadrūpābhāvebhyaḥ | BBs_3,4.40 |
body.translated_text: But for one who has become that (a renunciant), there is no reverting from that state — <s>Jaimini</s> also (agrees), because of the restriction, and because the characteristics of the former state are absent. (BBs 3.4.40)

body.text: na cādhikārikam api patanānumānāt tadayogāt | BBs_3,4.41 |
body.translated_text: Nor is it merely a qualification (for knowledge), because of the inference of falling (from the order), and because that (return) is impossible. (BBs 3.4.41)

body.text: upapūrvam apīty eke bhāvamaśanavat tad uktam | BBs_3,4.42 |
body.translated_text: Some (say) that even one who has taken the preceding (vow may renounce), like the state of fasting — that has been stated. (BBs 3.4.42)

body.text: bahis tūbhayathāpi smṛter ācārāc ca | BBs_3,4.43 |
body.translated_text: But one who is outside (the <s>āśramas</s>), in either case, because of <s>Smṛti</s> and conduct. (BBs 3.4.43)
The fruit belongs to the master (of the sacrifice), because of the scriptural statement of the result — thus says <s>Ātreya</s>. (BBs 3.4.44)

body.text: ārtvijyam ity auḍulomiḥ tasmai hi parikrīyate | BBs_3,4.45 |
body.translated_text: It belongs to the officiating priest (<s>ṛtvij</s>) — thus says <s>Auḍulomi</s> — for he is engaged for that purpose. (BBs 3.4.45)

body.text: sahakāryantaravidhiḥ pakṣeṇa tṛtīyaṃ tadvato vidhyādivat | BBs_3,4.46 |
body.translated_text: The injunction of an additional auxiliary applies optionally as the third (alternative), for one who possesses that (knowledge), like the injunction and similar cases. (BBs 3.4.46)
But the summing up is for the householder, because of the completeness (of all duties in that stage). (BBs 3.4.47)
Like the vow of silence, because of instruction for the others (other <s>āśramas</s>) also. (BBs 3.4.48)
Without revealing (himself as a knower), because of the connection (with concealment). (BBs 3.4.49)
The result in this life (is obtained) when there is no obstruction to what is intended, for thus it is seen (in scripture). (BBs 3.4.50)
Thus, there is no restriction regarding the fruit of liberation; this is established because that state is ascertained — because that state is ascertained. (BBs 3.4.51)
Repetition (of meditation is necessary), because of the repeated instruction (in scripture). (BBs 4.1.1)
And because of the indicatory marks. (BBs 4.1.2)
But they approach (it) as the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), and also teach (it) thus. (BBs 4.1.3)

body.text: na pratīke na hi saḥ | BBs_4,1.4 |
body.translated_text: Not in a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>), for He is not that. (BBs 4.1.4)
The vision of <s>Brahman</s> (should be superimposed on symbols), because of its superiority. (BBs 4.1.5)
And the meditations on <s>Āditya</s> and the like are to be applied to the subsidiary members (of rites), because this is reasonable. (BBs 4.1.6)
One should meditate while seated, because that is possible (in that posture). (BBs 4.1.7)
And because of (the nature of) meditation. (BBs 4.1.8)
And considering the requirement of steadiness (of posture). (BBs 4.1.9)
And the <s>Smṛtis</s> state (this). (BBs 4.1.10)
Wherever concentration (is achieved), there (one may meditate), since there is no distinction. (BBs 4.1.11)
Until death, for that too is seen (in scripture). (BBs 4.1.12)
Upon attaining that (knowledge), there is the non-attachment and destruction of the subsequent and prior sins respectively, for thus scripture declares. (BBs 4.1.13)

body.text: itarasyāpy evam asaṃśleṣaḥ pāte tu | BBs_4,1.14 |
body.translated_text: Of the other (good works) also, similarly there is non-attachment, but upon the exhaustion (of their results). (BBs 4.1.14)

body.text: anārabdhakārye eva tu pūrve tadavadheḥ | BBs_4,1.15 |
body.translated_text: But only those (prior karmas) whose effects have not yet begun (are destroyed), for that is the limit. (BBs 4.1.15)
But the <s>Agnihotra</s> and other (rites) are indeed for the production of that (knowledge), for thus it is seen (in scripture). (BBs 4.1.16)
Moreover, according to some, there are other (means) also, belonging to both (knowledge and works). (BBs 4.1.17)
For (scripture says) 'whatever one does with knowledge.' (BBs 4.1.18)

body.text: bhogena tv itare kṣapayitvātha saṃpadyate | BBs_4,1.19 |
body.translated_text: But through experience the others (who lack knowledge) exhaust (their karma) and then attain (Brahman). (BBs 4.1.19)
Speech is merged in mind, because it is seen (in scripture) and because of the scriptural word. (BBs 4.2.1)
For this very reason, all (organs merge) successively. (BBs 4.2.2)
That mind (merges) in <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath), as is known from the subsequent (scriptural passage). (BBs 4.2.3)
That (<s>Prāṇa</s> merges) in the ruler (the individual soul), because of the approach and other (indications). (BBs 4.2.4)
(The soul merges) in the elements, because scripture states so. (BBs 4.2.5)
Not in one (element alone), for scripture shows (otherwise). (BBs 4.2.6)
And the departure is the same (for the knower and the ignorant) up to the beginning of the journey; and (the knower does) not (return), having nourished immortality. (BBs 4.2.7)
Because of the merging in that (the Supreme), there is the designation of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration for the ignorant). (BBs 4.2.8)
It (the subtle body) is subtle, as is known from its measure, and because it is so perceived. (BBs 4.2.9)
Not by the destruction (of the subtle body at that point), therefore. (BBs 4.2.10)
The warmth (that remains in the body) belongs to this (soul) alone, and this is reasonable. (BBs 4.2.11)

body.text: pratiṣedhād iti cen na śārīrāt spaṣṭo hyekeṣām | BBs_4,2.12 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that because of the denial (of all awareness at death the soul does not depart with consciousness), no, because (the denial refers) to the embodied (state); for in some (recensions) it is explicit. (BBs 4.2.12)
And it is stated in <s>Smṛti</s>. (BBs 4.2.13)

body.text: tāni pare tathā hy āha | BBs_4,2.14 |
body.translated_text: Those (organs) follow (the soul) to the next (body), for thus (scripture) says. (BBs 4.2.14)
Without separation (from the soul), because of the scriptural statement. (BBs 4.2.15)

The shining forth of the light at the top of that (the heart), the door being illuminated by that; by the power of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), together with the remembrance of the path that is the continuation of that (meditation). (BBs 4.2.16)
Following the rays (of the sun, the soul departs). (BBs 4.2.17)

body.text: niśi neti cen na sambandhasya yāvaddehabhāvitvād darśayati ca | BBs_4,2.18 |
body.translated_text: If it be said that (departure is) not at night, no, because the connection (with the rays) lasts as long as the body endures; and (scripture) shows this. (BBs 4.2.18)
And therefore (departure is possible) even during the southern course (of the sun). (BBs 4.2.19)

body.text: yoginaḥ prati smaryete smārte caite | BBs_4,2.20 |
body.translated_text: And for the <s>yogins</s> both (paths) are recorded in <s>Smṛti</s>, and these are indeed <s>smārta</s> (based on tradition). (BBs 4.2.20)
By the path beginning with light (<s>arcis</s>), for that is well known (in scripture). (BBs 4.3.1)
(The soul goes) to <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) and then onwards, from the general and specific (descriptions in various texts). (BBs 4.3.2)
Beyond lightning is <s>Varuṇa</s>, because of the connection (stated in scripture). (BBs 4.3.3)
They are guides (<s>ātivāhikas</s>), because of the indicatory marks of that (in scripture). (BBs 4.3.4)
By the one connected with lightning alone (the soul is led) from there, for thus scripture states. (BBs 4.3.5)
To the effected <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Brahmaloka</s>) — so says <s>Bādari</s> — because such a journey is reasonable. (BBs 4.3.6)
And because it is specifically characterized (as a realm). (BBs 4.3.7)
But the designation (of <s>Brahman</s>) is because of proximity. (BBs 4.3.8)

body.text: kāryātyaye tadadhyakṣeṇa sahātaḥ param abhidhānāt | BBs_4,3.9 |
body.translated_text: Upon the dissolution of the effected (world of <s>Brahmā</s>), together with the ruler of that (world), (the soul goes) from there to the highest, as is declared (in scripture). (BBs 4.3.9)
And because of <s>Smṛti</s>. (BBs 4.3.10)
(The soul goes) to the Supreme — so says <s>Jaimini</s> — because that is the primary meaning. (BBs 4.3.11)
And because it is seen (in scripture). (BBs 4.3.12)
And there is no intention directed toward the effected (<s>Brahman</s>). (BBs 4.3.13)

body.text: apratīkālambanān nayatīti bādarāyaṇa ubhayathā ca doṣāt tatkratuś ca | BBs_4,3.14 |
body.translated_text: <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> (holds that the guides) lead those who do not meditate on symbols; and because there would be a defect in both cases (otherwise); and because of the principle of 'as one meditates, so one becomes' (<s>tatkratu</s>). (BBs 4.3.14)
And (scripture) shows a distinction (between the two kinds of meditators). (BBs 4.3.15)
Upon attaining (Brahman), there is manifestation (of the soul's own nature), according to its own scriptural word. (BBs 4.4.1)
(The soul is) liberated, because of the promise (in scripture). (BBs 4.4.2)
(What manifests is) the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), because of the context. (BBs 4.4.3)
In a state of non-separation (from <s>Brahman</s>), because it is so seen (in scripture). (BBs 4.4.4)
(The liberated soul exists) in the nature of <s>Brahman</s> — so says <s>Jaimini</s> — because of the references and other (reasons). (BBs 4.4.5)
As pure consciousness alone, since that is its essential nature — thus says <s>Auḍulomi</s>. (BBs 4.4.6)

body.text: evam apy upanyāsāt pūrvabhāvād avirodhaṃ bādarāyaṇaḥ | BBs_4,4.7 |
body.translated_text: Even so, because of the (scriptural) references and because of the prior state, there is no contradiction — so says <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>. (BBs 4.4.7)
By mere will (the liberated soul accomplishes everything), for thus scripture declares. (BBs 4.4.8)
And for this very reason, (the liberated soul has) no other lord. (BBs 4.4.9)

body.text: abhāvaṃ bādarir āha hy evam | BBs_4,4.10 |
body.translated_text: <s>Bādari</s> says there is absence (of body and organs for the liberated), for thus (scripture) declares. (BBs 4.4.10)
<s>Jaimini</s> says there is (a body and organs), because of the option (mentioned in scripture) and because of thinking (about it). (BBs 4.4.11)
Like the twelve-day sacrifice, it is of both kinds — so says <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, for this reason. (BBs 4.4.12)
In the absence of a body, (the fulfillment of desires is) like in a dream state, because this is reasonable. (BBs 4.4.13)
When there is a body, it is like the waking state. (BBs 4.4.14)
The entering (into bodies) is like a lamp (lighting other lamps), for thus (scripture) shows. (BBs 4.4.15)
(The passage about absence of all awareness refers to) one or the other of deep sleep and union (with <s>Brahman</s>), for that has been made manifest (in scripture). (BBs 4.4.16)
Except the activity of world-creation, because of the context, and because of the absence of proximity (of the liberated soul to the creative function). (BBs 4.4.17)
If it be said that (omnipotence is taught by) direct statement, no, because (it is said) with reference to the one presiding over the sphere of authority (<s>adhikārikamaṇḍala</s>). (BBs 4.4.18)

body.text: vikārāvarti ca tathā hi sthitim āha | BBs_4,4.19 |
body.translated_text: And (the liberated soul) is free from transformation (of <s>saṃsāra</s>), for thus (scripture) declares (its) abiding. (BBs 4.4.19)
And thus both direct perception and inference show (this). (BBs 4.4.20)
And because of the indicatory mark of equality only in enjoyment (not in creative power). (BBs 4.4.21)
There is no return, because of the scriptural word; there is no return, because of the scriptural word. (BBs 4.4.22)
